name: Splash Image Captcha
author: nikhilxpadwal113

sections.description:
Splash Image Captcha adds an “I’m not a robot” check to your forms. Visitors click it, pick the matching photos in a popup grid, and click Verify. The answer is checked on your server, which issues a short-lived pass token that the form must carry. Every supported form plugin re-checks that token server-side, so bots that skip the JavaScript are rejected.

It works right after activation with a built-in set of 95 free photos from Unsplash in 12 categories. No account or API key is needed.

Works with

  • Contact Form 7 — every form automatically, or only forms containing [splash_captcha]
  • Elementor Pro Forms — every form automatically, or through the “Image Captcha (Splash)” field type
  • Divi / Extra Contact Form module
  • WPForms (Lite and Pro)
  • Gravity Forms
  • Fluent Forms
  • Formidable Forms
  • WordPress login, registration, lost password and comment forms (including WooCommerce product reviews)
  • WooCommerce My Account login and registration
  • Your own forms — [splash_captcha] or splcap_render(), then check splcap_verify()

Features

  • Popup or inline challenge, 3×3, 4×3 or 4×4 grid.
  • Three photo sources: the built-in set, your own Unsplash API key (fresh photos daily), or images from your Media Library.
  • Cache-friendly: challenges load over the REST API when the visitor clicks, so full-page caching never serves stale tokens.
  • One attempt per challenge, a minimum solve time and per-IP rate limits (with real visitor IPs behind Cloudflare).
  • A solved check stays valid for 20 minutes and up to 3 submits, so a typo elsewhere in the form doesn’t force a new puzzle.
  • Light, dark or automatic theme, custom accent colour, keyboard accessible, optional text question for visitors who can’t use images.
  • If no photos are available, the widget falls back to a simple arithmetic question, so forms are never left unprotected.

External services

This plugin uses Unsplash, a free photo service, for the captcha images.

Unsplash image CDN (images.unsplash.com) — used with the “Built-in photos” and “Unsplash API” image sources (the default is Built-in photos).
* What is sent: when a visitor opens the captcha, their browser loads 9–16 photos directly from images.unsplash.com. Like any image request, this sends the visitor’s IP address, browser user agent and the page address (referrer) to Unsplash. No form data is sent.
* When: only after the visitor clicks the captcha checkbox (or tries to submit a protected form).
* Choosing “My Media Library” as the image source stops all requests to Unsplash.

Unsplash API (api.unsplash.com) — used only if you choose the “Unsplash API” image source and enter your own Access Key.
* What is sent: your site’s server sends your Access Key and each category keyword (for example “sailboat”) to search for photos, once when you save the settings and then once a day. No visitor data is sent.

  • Unsplash Terms of Service: https://unsplash.com/terms
  • Unsplash Privacy Policy: https://unsplash.com/privacy
  • Unsplash API Guidelines: https://help.unsplash.com/api-guidelines/unsplash-api-guidelines

Photographers are credited inside the captcha (the ⓘ button), as the Unsplash license and API guidelines ask.

Privacy

The plugin sets no cookies and stores no personal data in the database permanently. To rate-limit abuse it keeps a short-lived counter (10 minutes) keyed by a one-way hash of the visitor’s IP address, and each challenge is stored for up to 10 minutes. See “External services” for what Unsplash receives.
sections.installation:
1. Install from Plugins → Add New, or upload the zip, and activate.
  2. Go to Settings → Image Captcha. The built-in photos are already active.
  3. Tick the forms you want to protect and try the live preview on the same screen.

Optional: choose “Unsplash API” and paste a free Access Key from your Unsplash developer account, or choose “My Media Library” and pick at least 3 images per category.
sections.faq:
I locked myself out of wp-login.php

Add define( 'SPLCAP_DISABLE', true ); to wp-config.php. All checks are skipped until you remove it. The WordPress login integration is off by default because some page builders’ login widgets post to wp-login.php without printing the login_form hook.

Which categories work best?

Subjects that never share one photo. “Owl”, “teapot” and “tractor” work well; “car” and “street” produce ambiguous tiles. If visitors fail often, switch Strictness to “Forgiving”.

How strong is it?

It stops the automated spam that hits most WordPress forms. Like every image captcha, a determined attacker using a modern vision model can solve it. Combine it with your form plugin’s own anti-spam options for best results.

Does it work with page caching?

Yes. The page only contains an empty placeholder; the challenge is requested when the visitor clicks.

Custom forms

Print the widget inside your form with <?php splcap_render(); ?> (or the [splash_captcha] shortcode), and when handling the submission reject it if splcap_verify() returns false.

Hooks

  • splcap_skip_verification (bool) — bypass all checks.
  • splcap_verify_result (bool, $pass) — override a result.
  • splcap_pass_max_uses (int, default 3).
  • splcap_rate_limit_challenge / splcap_rate_limit_verify (int per 10 minutes per IP, default 40).
  • splcap_client_ip (string) — adjust how the visitor IP is detected.
  • splcap_js_targets (array) — extra CSS selectors for forms the script should add the widget to.
  • splcap_load_assets (bool) — control front-end asset loading.
  • JavaScript: a uic:verified event fires on the widget; window.SplashCaptcha.init() and window.SplashCaptcha.reset( container ).

  • Readme: updated the Unsplash Terms and Privacy links.
  • New plugin icon on the settings page.

1.4.0

  • First release on WordPress.org.
  • Built-in set of 95 free Unsplash photos — works without an API key.
  • Photo sources: built-in, Unsplash API, or Media Library.
  • Popup or inline challenge.
  • Support for Contact Form 7, Elementor Pro, Divi, WPForms, Gravity Forms, Fluent Forms, Formidable, WooCommerce and WordPress core forms.
